body: this is from #6306 which I kind of figured would cause a regression, but I thought it would be that people were using timezone=True on their `DateTime` type, which fortunately is not what you're doing here.

note UTC isnt being "converted" here, it's just being dropped.

also there seems to be a loss of microseconds precision using the driver.

> there seems to be a loss of microseconds precision using the driver.

Yes that is ok. Always been like that with pyodbc

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Pass all datetime values to pyodbc for timezone-naive column** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2779

**Describe the bug**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->

When using a [sqlalchemy custom type](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/core/custom_types.html) the incorrect data type is being generated in the migrations.

I'm using the following custom type to store and load datetime objects with utc.

```python
class TZTimestamp(TypeDecorator):
    """A new sqlalchemy column that is timezone aware

    Uses TIMESTAMP or datetime2
    """

    impl = TypeEngine  # placeholder since we use load_dialect_impl
    cache_ok = True

    def load_dialect_impl(self, dialect):
        if dialect.name == "mssql":
            return dialect.type_descriptor(DATETIMEOFFSET())
        else:
            return dialect.type_descriptor(TIMESTAMP())

    def process_bind_param(self, value, dialect):
        # prevent storing unaware datetimes
        # if not isinstance(value, datetime.datetime):
        #     raise ValueError(f"{value} must be a datetime.datetime")
        if isinstance(value, datetime.datetime) and value.tzinfo is None:
            raise ValueError(f"{value} must be TZ-aware")
        # # convert the value to utc time
        # value = value.astimezone(pytz.UTC)

        if dialect.name == "mssql":
            return value.isoformat()

        return value

    def process_result_value(self, value, engine):
        # make returned datetimes timezone aware (they are already utc)
        return value.replace(tzinfo=pytz.UTC)
```

The `load_dialect_impl` function is used to fallback on a `DateTimeOffset()` implementation for mssql and otherwise use a `Timestamp()`.

For some reason the mssql data type generated by alembic is a `datetime`.

**Expected behavior**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->

The mssql data type would be a `DateTimeOffset()`

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

When setting the `UTCDate` field in MsSQL, using mssql PyODBC driver as of 1.4.10 fails to update datetime with timezone.

NOTE! While the problem is very similar to one described in #6366, (including identical error), it has not been fixed in 1.4.12, when #6366 has been merged. I believe the problem is that the behaviour described there related to INSERT, our problem in Apache Airflow is about UPDATE.

The problem is that when the UTCDateTime field is updated in MSSQL with PyODBC driver, the value gets converted to string and the string fails to be converted to Date.

The field is defined as UTCDateTime: 

https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/d353f023ff8856c00b9f054526cb2e40ff0116ae/airflow/models/taskinstance.py#L376

We set the field in one of our tests to ```timezone.utcnow() - datetime.timedelta(seconds=60)```

https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/d353f023ff8856c00b9f054526cb2e40ff0116ae/tests/jobs/test_scheduler_job.py#L3467

The subsequent `session.flush()` generates an error message: 

> Conversion failed when converting date and/or time from character string. (241) (SQLExecDirectW)')

Caused by this query:
```
UPDATE task_instance SET state=?, trigger_timeout=? WHERE task_instance.task_id = ? AND task_instance.dag_id = ? AND task_instance.run_id = ? AND task_instance.map_index = ?'                                                                  
parameters = ((<TaskInstanceState.DEFERRED: 'deferred'>, '2022-02-02 15:04:07.013951 +00:00', 'dummy1', 'test_timeout_triggers', 't...tanceState.DEFERRED: 'deferred'>, '2022-02-02 15:06:07.013964 +00:00', 'dummy1', 'test_timeout_triggers', 'test2', -1))
```

We bisected the problem and the test clearly stops working in  1.4.10 (1.4.9 is fine) and all versions from 1.4.10 until latest released 1.4.31 exhibit the same problem. NOTE - SQLAlchemy 1.3 works fine as well.

You can see an example failure in CI here: https://github.com/apache/airflow/runs/5027548731?check_suite_focus=true

We are going to temporarily limit SQLAlchemy to <1.4.10 to contain the issue (it breaks our PRs currently) but it would be great to fix it soon-ish so that we can use latest and greates SQLAlchmy (MSSQL is not yet offixially released by Apache Airflow but we plan to do it in ~ 2 months and this issue is effectively blocking us from upgrading SQLAlchemy also for MySQL and Postgres as we keep one version of dependencies for our package - regardless of the database used).


### To Reproduce

1) Clone Apache Airflow GitHub project (https://github.com/apache/airflow/) 

2) In the repository, run `./breeze --github-image-id 2652c6ef435e501e171062398874b38c375f9403 --backend mssql --python 3.9 --db-reset --skip-mounting-local-sources --test-type Core  shell` 

This will bring up a complete development environment with Airflow + MSSQL database via docker-compose (you need to have modern docker and docker-compose installed). It might take few minutes (depending on your network speed) to download the images and start `breeze` environment (MacOS/Linux are supported as Host environment in general)

3) Once this is complete, you get into the `Breeze` shell you should be able to run the tests:

```
root@a6c901f19630:/opt/airflow# 
```

4) Check your SQLALchemy version (should be 1.4.31)

```
root@a6c901f19630:/opt/airflow# pip freeze | grep SQLAlchemy
Flask-SQLAlchemy==2.5.1
SQLAlchemy==1.4.31
SQLAlchemy-JSONField==1.0.0
SQLAlchemy-Utils==0.38.2
root@a6c901f19630:/opt/airflow# 
```

5) You can run the test that failed:

pytest tests/jobs/test_scheduler_job.py::TestSchedulerJob::test_timeout_triggers

It should throw an error:
```
ERROR tests/jobs/test_scheduler_job.py::TestSchedulerJob::test_timeout_triggers - sqlalchemy.exc.PendingRollbackError: This Session's transaction has been rolled back due to a previous exception during flush. To begin a new transaction with this Session, first issue Session.rollback(). Original except...
FAILED tests/jobs/test_scheduler_job.py::TestSchedulerJob::test_timeout_triggers - sqlalchemy.exc.DataError: (pyodbc.DataError) ('22007', '[22007] [Microsoft][ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server][SQL Server]Conversion failed when converting date and/or time from character string. (241) (SQLExecDirectW)')
=================================================================================================================================== 1 failed, 40 warnings, 1 error in 12.67s ====================================================================================================================================
```


6) Update to SQLALchemy 1.4.9
```
pip install SQLAlchemy==1.4.9
```

7) Re-run the test:

```
pytest tests/jobs/test_scheduler_job.py::TestSchedulerJob::test_timeout_triggers
```

It should succed this time

```
====== 1 passed, 34 warnings in 12.00s =====
```

You can install other versions (including 1.4.12 which was supposed to fix #6366 which seems very closely related). Both #6366 and this one were introduced in 1.4.10.

issue.body:
SQL Alchemy 1.4.10 introduces a bug where for PyODBC driver UTCDateTime
fields get wrongly converted as string and fail to be converted back to
datetime. It was supposed to be fixed in
https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/6366 (released in
1.4.10) but apparently our case is different.

Opened https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/7660 to track it
